label: Late original phase / <DEL> in sequences that start with z, b or 0
explanation: Fires only from step 3 up to the <DEL> step: in the second half of the original phase (peak rate at orig_idx 5-7) and on <DEL> itself (23% of delimiter steps, 27% of mass). It essentially never fires at t<3 or during copying (1% of mass, mostly the first copy step). How often and how strongly it fires depends on the first one or two original tokens. Sequences starting with z or b have about 5x lift and hold nearly half the mass, and 0 is next at 2.4x. The strongest examples (0.7-1.0 of max) are sequences like z b z ... or b z ..., where activation rises over steps 4-7 and peaks at or just before <DEL>. The input token at the current step barely matters. Weak activations below 0.3 of max also show up in late original-phase steps of sequences with other first tokens, and the predicate misses these. Test-split result: the predicate covers about 97% of top-quartile activations but only about 20-30% of the bottom half.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: z, b, 0, e, s, w; least: o, v, i, x) and the second original token (most: z, b, s, 0, w, m; least: o, v, i, x); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=6, t=4.
